title: Settings
desc: Account security, access control, runtime parameters, backup and migration, and system information

restartBanner.title: Some settings require a restart to take effect
restartBanner.desc: Changes such as the listen address have been saved and take effect after Gately restarts.

admin.title: Administrator account
admin.help: All signed-in sessions are invalidated after the change; you will need to sign in again.
admin.mismatch: The new passwords do not match

totp.title: Two-factor authentication
totp.enabledDesc: Signing in requires a 6-digit code from your authenticator app in addition to the password.
totp.scanDesc: Scan the QR code with an app such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, then enter the displayed code to confirm.
totp.manualHint: Enter this key manually if you cannot scan
totp.introDesc: Once enabled, signing in also requires a one-time code from your authenticator app, protecting the console even if your password leaks.
totp.disablePrompt: Enter your current password and the 6-digit code from your authenticator to turn off two-factor authentication.
totp.autoHint: Submitted automatically once the password and all 6 digits are entered

loginProtect.title: Login protection
loginProtect.sessionHoursHelp: Hours; sign in again after this period
loginProtect.maxFailuresHelp: Lock a source after this many consecutive wrong passwords; 0 uses the default

thirdLogin.title: Third-party sign-in
thirdLogin.desc: Sign in to the console with a GitHub, Google, QQ or any OIDC account. Uses your own OAuth apps; the sign-in flow never goes through a relay server.
thirdLogin.callbackBasePlaceholder: https://gately.example.com (the address you use in the browser to open the console, without a path)
thirdLogin.callbackHelp: The callback URL to register on each platform is {url}. Sign-in must be started after opening the console from this address.
thirdLogin.allowedPlaceholder: One per line: provider:account, e.g. github:15172899 or google:me{'@'}gmail.com; add a note after # at the end of a line
thirdLogin.allowedHelp: Only accounts in this list can sign in. For GitHub, a numeric ID is recommended. When a QQ sign-in is rejected the first time, the page shows an identifier you can copy.
thirdLogin.skipTotpHelp: When two-factor authentication is enabled, turning this on stops third-party sign-in from asking for a code; turning it off rejects third-party sign-in

apiToken.title: API tokens
apiToken.desc: API tokens now support multiple tokens with fine-grained permissions: create several tokens, each with its own expiry and read-only / read-write access per module.

listen.title: Console listener
listen.httpsHelp: The certificate is chosen by access domain from "SSL certificates"
listen.forceHttpsHelp: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS automatically (only when the certificate module has a certificate for the domain)

restrict.title: Access restrictions
restrict.safePathHelp: Once set, you must visit {url} to open the console; any other path returns 404, which keeps scanners from finding the console. Remember your entry address.
restrict.lanOnlyHelp: Allow only LAN addresses (including Tailscale 100.64.0.0/10 addresses) to access the console
restrict.gatewaySSOHelp: When Gately is opened from the fnOS desktop icon, a signed-in fnOS administrator is signed in to Gately as the administrator without a password or two-step code. Regular fnOS users still need to sign in.
restrict.trustProxyHelp: When the admin UI sits behind nginx, haproxy or Gately Web Services on this host, take the real client address from the X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers they set. Used for LAN-only access, sign-in rate limiting and the audit log. Headers are only trusted from addresses of this host.
restrict.trustedProxiesHelp: Proxy addresses outside this host, such as a Docker bridge gateway or another reverse proxy server.

deny.label: Unauthorized response

help.default: Requests that miss the security entrance get a Gately-branded notice page (404); requests blocked by LAN-only access or from banned sources get 403.
help.notfound: Returns a generic 404 page with no product information, like an ordinary web server with nothing on it.
help.blank: Returns an empty page with status 200.
help.close: Closes the connection without sending anything. When a public source is blocked by LAN-only access or a ban, the connection is closed right after it is accepted, so the HTTPS port does not even send its certificate. Requests forwarded by a reverse proxy get the plain 404 instead, so the proxy does not show its own error page.
help.drop: Never answers the request; the client waits until it times out (each connection is held for at most 2 minutes, up to 256 at a time; extra ones are closed). When a public source is blocked by LAN-only access or a ban, the HTTPS port does not send its certificate either. Requests forwarded by a reverse proxy get the plain 404 instead, so the proxy does not show its own error page.
help.custom: Returns the HTML page and status code below, for example the default page of some other kind of website.

deny.pageHelp: The page is shown in a browser sandbox: scripts, forms and external resources (images, stylesheets, font files) do not load. Inline images and fonts as data: URLs and put styles in a style tag.
deny.sampleConfirm: Replace the current content with the sample page?
deny.warnEntry: A mistyped security entrance no longer shows the notice page. If you forget the entrance, clear safePath in gately.json in the config directory and restart Gately.
deny.warnPort: The TCP port is still open and port scans can still find it. To hide the port completely, restrict sources with a firewall or remove the public port mapping.
deny.warnNoTrigger: No security entrance is set and LAN-only access is off, so this setting only applies to banned sources.

network.title: Network
network.dnsPlaceholder: Leave empty to use system DNS; enter an IP or IP:port
network.dnsHelp: Affects all outbound name resolution (DDNS, Webhook, ACME, etc.). With multiple servers, one is picked at random with automatic failover.
network.updateProxyHelp: Used to reach GitHub when checking for updates and upgrading online. Supports http://, https:// and socks5://; when empty, the HTTPS_PROXY environment variable is honored.
network.timeZoneHelp: Time zone used for logs, scheduled tasks and more. Any IANA time zone name is accepted. Currently in effect: {zone}
network.serverLanguageHelp: Language for logs, notifications and other output with no page context. When empty, it follows the system environment (GATELY_LANG, LANG); if the environment sets no language, it follows the language of the most recent admin console login.
network.autoUpdateCheckHelp: Contacts GitHub every 12 hours to check for new Gately versions and security advisories, and checks installed managed programs; findings appear at the top of the page and are sent according to your Notifications rules. Requests are anonymous and upload nothing.

runtime.title: Runtime parameters
runtime.logLinesHelp: Number of log lines each module keeps in memory; with log persistence on they are restored from disk after a restart
runtime.logPersistHelp: Write runtime logs to logs/ in the config directory so they survive restarts; when off, logs are kept in memory only
runtime.logFileMBHelp: Each module's log file is rotated when full and one previous file is kept, so it uses at most twice this size; 0 means the default of 2 MB
runtime.gcPercentHelp: 0 means default (100); lowering it reduces memory use but increases CPU overhead
runtime.maxProcsHelp: 0 means automatic ({count} cores on this machine)

restart.title: Restart
restart.desc: The console and all forwarding and proxy services are briefly interrupted during a restart (usually a few seconds).
restart.confirm: The console and all forwarding and proxy services are briefly interrupted during a restart (usually a few seconds). Restart Gately?

modules.title: Modules
modules.desc: Turn on only the modules you need. A disabled module starts no services, serves no admin API and is hidden from the UI; its configuration is kept and comes back when you turn it on again. Modules that others depend on cannot be disabled.
modules.backupDesc: Back up all configuration to local disk or storage on a schedule

save.savedNeedRestart: Saved. Some settings take effect after a restart

import.title: Import from Lucky
import.desc: Supports {lkcf} files (multiple allowed) from the Lucky configuration directory (Docker default {dir}), and whole-site backups exported from the Lucky console ({zip}). Preview first, then import after confirming. Imported entries are appended after existing ones; entries with the same name are skipped.
import.dragHint: .lkcf config files or a whole-site backup .zip
import.keepEnableTitle: Keep the enabled state from Lucky after import
import.keepEnableDesc: Off by default: all imported rules are disabled, so you can enable them one by one after checking. When on, rules enabled in Lucky will {bold}. If Lucky is still running, port conflicts may occur or both sides may update records at the same time.
import.keepEnableBold: start listening on ports and updating DNS records immediately
import.previewDone: Preview complete. Import once everything looks right
import.noModules: No modules supported by Gately were found
import.confirmKeep: {total} entries will be imported with their enabled state from Lucky: enabled rules take effect immediately. Continue?
import.confirmDisabled: {total} entries will be imported, all disabled after import. Continue?

backup.title: Back up Gately configuration
backup.desc: Download a zip file containing the full configuration (account, rules, certificates, etc.). The backup contains password hashes, secrets and certificate private keys, so store it safely.

restore.title: Restore configuration
restore.desc: Use a backup zip to {bold}. The current configuration is first saved to a backup-timestamp folder in the config directory, and Gately restarts automatically after the restore.
restore.confirm: All current configuration will be overwritten with "{name}" and Gately will restart automatically. The current configuration is backed up to the config directory first. Type "{word}" to confirm.
restore.success: Restored {count} configuration files; the previous configuration is saved at {previous}
